content: For newly diagnosed adults suspected of having Type 8 diabetes, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends an age-based diagnostic pathway that includes the evaluation of C-peptide levels. 1. If the C-peptide level is greater than 600 pmol/L, the diagnosis is most likely Type 2 diabetes. 2. If the C-peptide level falls between 200 and 600 pmol/L, the result is considered indeterminate. In such cases, it is advisable to consider repeating the C-peptide test after a period of five years to reassess the diagnosis. 3. If the C-peptide level is less than 200 pmol/L, the diagnosis is most likely Type 1 diabetes.
